text: Bronze is landed. Now you'll write the transformation that turns that untouched raw data into the clean, typed, deduplicated Silver table Lesson Two's plan called for.

Starting from bronze dot daily sales raw, this calls dropDuplicates on order id and line number -- the real business key for a sale line item -- casts sale date to a real date and sales amount to a real decimal, and filters out any row missing store id, sale date, or sales amount.

The result writes out as silver dot sales transactions, in overwrite mode, because Silver recomputes from the entirety of Bronze every single run -- it doesn't need its own history, just to be correct right now.

Three choices here are worth understanding, not just copying. Naming order id and line number as the dedup key catches real duplicate line items, where a plain dropDuplicates with no arguments would miss anything that differs in even one unrelated column. The explicit casts matter because next lesson's aggregation needs sales amount to actually be a number it can sum, not a string that merely looks like one. And overwrite mode is a real, named limitation -- it means every run recomputes everything from scratch, which a later, more advanced version of this pipeline would fix with a Delta merge instead.
That's Silver, built and clean. Next lesson, you'll aggregate it down into the one number per day that this whole project was actually asked for.
